reconstruction.scope: Standing rebuilt Dharahara: pale tapered circular shaft with eight molded collars/sparse circular oculi, actual recessed arched base entrance/closed dark door, projecting molded observation deck/open balustrade, shallow domed lantern and slender finial. Separate mapped stepped old base, irregular broken brick/plaster stump under an open-framed translucent pyramidal shelter. Original simple trim/rail/radial support vocabulary, shared textures and four browser levels. No reconstruction of the destroyed full historical tower, copied inscription/photo atlas, furnished interior, underground museum, broad precinct plaza or temporary lights/visitors.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Use the two inspected2026 picture captions as nominal72m current rebuilt tower height, including top finial; this is not a survey. Retain old unqualified61.88m catalog fact as historical/ambiguous, not overwrite it or apply it to the rebuilt tower. Map components give51m body,61m upper body and58–63m crown; pictured proportions guide body taper/roughly60m balcony/rounded lantern and72m needle. Main footprint diameter15.33m controls base size; top shaft diameter9.7m, observation rim13.6m are picture/map estimates. Older stepped base is map-height0.5–4m, brown broken stump to about8m and protective glass pyramid to12.5m above its local base. Sparse oculus schedule, rail count, damaged rim, glazing frame/entrance detail and exact heights remain simplified visual estimates.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Keep original standard6m Mapzen grid, all independent buildings, native paths/water unchanged. Replace only the thirteen corresponding tower/old-base map shells with2cm cut tolerance. Each circular occupied footing has buried retaining sides and a separately grade-fitted local floor; narrow entrance treads are supported over native grade. No whole-precinct slab, ground/water cutout or terrain flattening. Coarse DEM does not resolve actual plaza, foundations or underground museum: absolute levels, footing rise and old shelter/stump height are visualization contact estimates.
